passage:
Tuesday, 11.40 pm, finally home.
Okay. Deep breath. I'm still shaking a little. Coming back from the late shift, a police jeep flashed its light at me near the flyover and an officer waved me to the side. My heart was BANGING. My first thought was to walk faster. I didn't. I kept both hands where they could see them, said "Good evening," and held out my ID before they asked. "May I know why I've been stopped?" It was a routine check. The officer looked at my ID, asked where I was going, and let me go in two minutes. I had Anjali on a call the whole time with the phone in my pocket, and she stayed quiet and listened. She says I did everything right. 🙂 I'm going to sleep now.

qa.q: Where was the diary writer stopped by the police jeep?
What was the diary writer feeling when the officer waved to the side?
qa.a: Fear, since the heart was banging and the first urge was to walk faster.

qa.q: What helped the stop go smoothly?
qa.a: Keeping both hands visible, being polite, showing ID, asking calmly why the stop happened and having Anjali on the call.

qa.q: How might Anjali have felt listening on the phone during the stop?
qa.a: Probably anxious and helpless, but she stayed quiet so the writer could focus, and afterwards she was proud.

grounding: Stopped at night by police, the protagonist is afraid but stays calm, keeps hands visible, is polite, shows ID, asks the reason and has someone on the phone.
